title: 首页哪个位置是否可以显示一下当前版本？
Streaming collector rejects MiMo's repetition_truncation finish reason
body:
## Problem Description

While evaluating MiMo V2.6 Flash with thinking disabled, two responses completed with HTTP 200 and SSE `[DONE]` but failed before prediction caching. MiMo returned `finish_reason="repetition_truncation"`, which its [API schema](https://mimo.mi.com/docs/en-US/api/chat/openai-api) documents as repetition detection. EvalScope rejected it while constructing the OpenAI SDK's `Choice`.

The HLE run stopped with 16 of 24 predictions saved. A separate transport failure also occurred during that run; this report concerns the completed responses rejected during stream assembly.

## EvalScope Version (Required)

1.8.1 at `fce1d21391dc2d7b45c9cf0edb9b9e40d526aed3`, with OpenAI 2.54.0 and HTTPX 0.28.1.

## Tools Used

Native framework, OpenAI-compatible model API.

## Executed Code or Instructions

The live generation used `stream=true`, `thinking={"type":"disabled"}`, temperature 0, and a 32,768-token cap.

The following standalone reproduction needs no key or dataset. Only the HTTP response is a fixture; the OpenAI SSE parser and EvalScope collector are real. I also reproduced this through a loopback HTTP server and the native evaluation path.

Run this in an environment with the versions above:

```python
import json
import httpx
from openai import OpenAI
from pydantic import ValidationError
from evalscope.models.utils.openai import collect_stream_response

for reason in ('stop', 'repetition_truncation'):
    chunk = {'id': 'fixture', 'created': 1, 'model': 'fixture',
             'object': 'chat.completion.chunk', 'choices': [{'index': 0,
             'delta': {'role': 'assistant', 'content': 'retained answer'},
             'finish_reason': reason}]}
    body = f'data: {json.dumps(chunk)}\n\ndata: [DONE]\n\n'
    transport = httpx.MockTransport(lambda request: httpx.Response(
        200, headers={'content-type': 'text/event-stream'}, content=body))
    with OpenAI(api_key='EMPTY', http_client=httpx.Client(transport=transport)) as client:
        with client.chat.completions.create(model='fixture', stream=True,
                messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': 'answer'}]) as stream:
            try:
                completion, _ = collect_stream_response(response_stream=stream)
                print(f'{reason}: content={completion.choices[0].message.content!r}')
            except ValidationError as error:
                print(f'{reason}: {error}')
```

## Error Log

Observed output from that snippet:

```text
stop: content='retained answer'
repetition_truncation: 1 validation error for Choice
finish_reason
  Input should be 'stop', 'length', 'tool_calls', 'content_filter' or 'function_call' [type=literal_error, input_value='repetition_truncation', input_type=str]
    For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.13/v/literal_error
```

## Running Environment

Python 3.12. The live failure occurred on a Linux GitHub Actions runner; the standalone reproduction above ran on macOS.

## Additional Information

At inspected main revision `06b4c67bc37d5482bdcca8b7a3dee335b9e6b5a7`, both the [sync collector](https://github.com/modelscope/evalscope/blob/06b4c67bc37d5482bdcca8b7a3dee335b9e6b5a7/evalscope/models/utils/openai.py#L922-L924) and [async collector](https://github.com/modelscope/evalscope/blob/06b4c67bc37d5482bdcca8b7a3dee335b9e6b5a7/evalscope/models/utils/openai.py#L1055-L1057) still construct the strict `Choice`. That revision was inspected, not tested as a full installation.

Expected behavior: retain the returned answer and exact provider finish reason for evaluation. EvalScope's native `unknown` stop reason could represent repetition without claiming a normal stop, token-budget exhaustion, or content filtering. Supporting this documented value should preserve validation of other fields and must not admit incomplete streams or repair the answer.

title: math_equal accepts any numeric answer off by exactly 100x (include_percentage defaults True), so gsm8k / math_500 grade 1800 == 18 as correct
body:
## Self-Check List

- [x] I have carefully read the relevant user documentation
- [x] I have reviewed the Frequently Asked Questions
- [x] I have searched and reviewed existing issues to confirm this is not a duplicate problem (adjacent, different defects: #1536/#1537, #1628/#1630)

## Problem Description

`math_equal` accepts any numeric prediction that is exactly 100x larger or smaller than the reference, on every numeric item, because `include_percentage` defaults to `True` and the `/100`, `*100` alternatives are built unconditionally. `Accuracy(numeric=True)` and `MathAcc` call it with defaults, so `gsm8k` and `math_500` score e.g. `1800` as equal to `18`.

`evalscope/metrics/math/parser.py:351-389` at `06b4c67` (also in v1.12.0):

```python
def math_equal(
    prediction,
    reference,
    include_percentage: bool = True,
    ...
):
    ...
    try:  # 1. numerical equal
        if is_digit(prediction) and is_digit(reference):
            prediction = parse_digits(prediction)
            reference = parse_digits(reference)
            # number questions
            if include_percentage:
                gt_result = [reference / 100, reference, reference * 100]
            else:
                gt_result = [reference]
            for item in gt_result:
                ...
                        if numeric_equal(prediction, item):
                            return True
```

The fan-out at `:375-376` does not check whether either side carried a `%`, and `parse_digits` (`:317`) already converts `18%` to `0.18` on its own, so the fan-out is not needed for the percent case it was written for. `Accuracy(numeric=True)` (`metrics/nlp/metrics.py:52-58`) and `MathAcc` (`:72-80`) call `math_equal(prediction, ref_answer)` with defaults; `gsm8k_adapter.py:69` and `math_500_adapter.py:49` both register `metric_list=[{'acc': {'numeric': True}}]` and neither overrides `match_score`. AIME is unaffected only because `aime_adapter.py:165-176` routes `match_score` to `benchmarks/aime/grader.py` instead.

## EvalScope Version (Required)

main `06b4c67` (2026-09-21); the same code is in v1.12.0.

## Tools Used

- [x] Native / Native framework

## Executed Code or Instructions

`math_equal` loaded from `evalscope/metrics/math/parser.py` (the `regex` module aliased to stdlib `re`, which it only uses for `regex.sub`/`regex.match`; `sympy` stubbed, safe because the numeric branch returns before the symbolic branch is reached):

| prediction | reference | include_percentage | result | expected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `'500'` | `'5'` | default (True) | **True** | False |
| `'0.05'` | `'5'` | default | **True** | False |
| `'42'` | `'4200'` | default | **True** | False |
| `'1800'` | `'18'` | default | **True** | False |
| `'0.18'` | `'18'` | default | **True** | False |
| `'6'` | `'5'` | default | False | False (control) |
| `'50'` | `'5'` | default | False | False (control, 10x) |
| `'18'` | `'18'` | default | True | True (control) |
| `'18.0'` | `'18'` | default | True | True (intended use) |
| `'18%'` | `'0.18'` | default | True | True (intended use) |
| `'18%'` | `'0.18'` | False | True | True (percent still handled by `parse_digits`) |
| `'500'` | `'5'` | False | False | False |

No test in `tests/` exercises `include_percentage`, `math_equal`, or `Accuracy(numeric=True)`, and nothing in the repo passes `include_percentage=False`.

## Error Log

No error is raised; the wrong verdict is silent. In the per-sample output `extracted_prediction` shows `1800`, the reference shows `18`, and `acc` shows `1.0`.

## Consequence

On gsm8k and math_500 a model whose final number is off by exactly two decimal places (a dropped or doubled percent conversion, dollars vs cents, a misplaced decimal) is scored `acc=1.0`. Because it fires on every numeric item, not only percent-shaped ones, reported accuracy is a strict upper bound on the true one and the inflation is invisible in the results.

## Suggested fix

Follow the AIME grader (`benchmarks/aime/grader.py:129-142`), which strips `%` / `\%` during normalization and then compares values directly with no x100 tolerance. In `math_equal`, only build the `reference / 100` and `reference * 100` alternatives when the raw `prediction` or `reference` string contains `%` (or `\%`); otherwise `gt_result = [reference]`. Note that `strip_answer_string` / `extract_answer` strip `%` before the comparison, so the flag has to be carried out of those helpers, or `include_percentage=False` passed for benchmarks whose references are never percentages (gsm8k targets are plain numbers after `####`). Tests: `math_equal('500', '5') is False`, `math_equal('1800', '18') is False`, `math_equal('18%', '0.18') is True`.

A related edge in the same function: `math_equal('', '')` returns `True` from the first `strip().lower()` comparison at `:365`, so an extraction failure against a blank reference scores 1.0; guarding on empty strings first, as `Accuracy(allow_inclusion=True)` already does with `bool(prediction) and ...` at `metrics.py:49`, closes it.

Happy to open the PR.

## Running Environment

macOS 15, Python 3.12, evalscope main `06b4c67` (source checkout).

title: AlpacaEval scores a win as 0.75 and a loss as 0.25 since v1.11.0
body:
## Self-Check List

Before submitting an issue, please ensure you have completed the following steps:
- [ ] I have carefully read the [relevant user documentation](https://evalscope.readthedocs.io/en/latest/get_started/parameters.html)
- [ ] I have reviewed the [Frequently Asked Questions](https://evalscope.readthedocs.io/en/latest/get_started/faq.html)
- [x] I have searched and reviewed existing issues to confirm this is not a duplicate problem

## Problem Description

Since v1.11.0, AlpacaEval counts a win as 0.75 and a loss as 0.25. Before v1.11.0, a win was 1 and a loss was 0. The official AlpacaEval also uses 1 and 0.

As a result, the reported win rate is 0.25 + 0.5 * p, where p is the true win rate. A model that wins 8 of 10 comparisons gets 0.65 instead of 0.80. A model that loses every comparison still gets 0.25.

The cause is the refactor in #1601. The reduce step in alpaca_eval_adapter.py creates the pairwise outcomes without a strength value, so they fall back to "weak". PairwiseOutcome.score gives 0.75 for a weak win and 0.25 for a weak loss. That scale fits Arena-Hard labels such as A>B, but the AlpacaEval judge only answers m or M.

## EvalScope Version (Required)

v1.12.0. v1.11.0 and v1.11.1 behave the same way. I also checked main at 06b4c67.

## Tools Used
- [x] Native / Native framework
- [ ] Opencompass backend
- [ ] VLMEvalKit backend
- [ ] RAGEval backend
- [ ] Perf / Model inference stress testing tool
- [ ] Arena / Arena mode

## Executed Code or Instructions

Run this from the repository root. It uses the scripted judge from the unit tests, so no API key is needed.

```python
from evalscope.api.registry import get_benchmark
from evalscope.config import TaskConfig
from tests.api.judge.test_migrated_adapters import ScriptedJudge, make_state

config = TaskConfig(model='m', datasets=['alpaca_eval'], judge={'strategy': 'llm', 'models': [{'model_id': 'j'}]})
for reply in ['{"verdict": "M"}', '{"verdict": "m"}']:
    adapter = get_benchmark('alpaca_eval', config)
    adapter.llm_judge = ScriptedJudge([reply])
    score = adapter.calculate_metrics(make_state('candidate', 'baseline')).score
    print(reply, score.value)
```

## Error Log

There is no error, but the scores are wrong:

```
{"verdict": "M"} {'win_rate': 0.75}
{"verdict": "m"} {'win_rate': 0.25}
```

The expected values are 1.0 and 0.0.

## Running Environment

- Operating System: macOS 26 (arm64)
- Python Version: 3.11.6

## Additional Information

I have a small fix with tests and will open a PR for it.

title: 是否接入jev类选择模型
body:
## 功能描述 / Feature Description
希望 EvalScope 支持接入 TypeSafe 的 Jev 模型，并将其作为评测执行模型，用于 MMLU、CMMLU、C-Eval 等多项选择类评测集。

## 需求背景 / Background

传统选择题评测通常依赖模型生成文本，再从文本中解析 A/B/C/D 等答案。这种方式可能受到额外解释文本、输出格式和答案解析规则的影响。
根据 TypeSafe 官方介绍，Jev 的 Choice 原语可以直接返回选项、概率分布和 confidence，无需先生成自然语言再解析结果。这一能力与 MMLU 等选择类评测任务非常匹配：
- 减少答案文本解析带来的不确定性；
- 直接获得结构化的选项结果；
- 可以保留概率和 confidence 信息；
- 适合作为 EvalScope 中的独立评测执行模型。

## 预期行为 / Expected Behavior
希望支持类似以下命令：
export TYPESAFE_API_KEY=your_api_key

evalscope eval \
  --model jev-latest \
  --eval-type jev_api \
  --datasets mmlu \
  --limit 5
具体期望包括：
1. 新增 Jev 模型 API 适配器，并接入 EvalScope 现有的模型注册机制。
2. 支持通过 TYPESAFE_API_KEY 配置认证信息。
3. 将评测样本中的题目、选项和必要上下文转换为 Jev API 所需的 state。
4. 使用 Jev 的 Choice 能力完成多项选择题评测。
5. 将 Jev 返回的选择结果转换为 EvalScope 统一的模型输出格式，例如 A、B、C、D。
6. 保留 Jev 返回的概率分布和 confidence，便于结果分析。
7. 兼容 EvalScope 现有的并发、超时、重试、缓存和评测报告机制。
8. 对不适用于 Jev 的传统生成参数进行明确说明，或安全忽略。
9. 增加单元测试和至少一个选择类 benchmark 的 smoke test。
10. 补充使用文档，说明模型配置、API Key、支持的 benchmark 以及限制条件。

## 其他信息 / Additional Information

Jev 官方介绍：https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction

## 功能描述 / Feature Description

希望在压测的多模态数据集类型中加入支持一次输入多张图片的数据集模式

## 需求背景 / Background

我方在使用evalscope进行压测时需要在一次请求中输入多张图片，同时不使用random_vl随机生成，因此需要evalscope支持一种一次可输入多张图片的数据集模式。现有的flickr8k和kontext_bench两种多模态数据集模式都是一次只能输入一张图片。

## 预期行为 / Expected Behavior

使用evalscope进行压测时支持使用一次可输入多张图片的开源数据集，并可根据此模式自行构造数据集。

title: ticket: Reliability, recovery, and scoped access
body:
## Parent

#1734 — spec: AI Compute Compass V1

## What to build

Compass remains explainable across database outages, event backlogs, blocked Deployments, cancellation, and authorization boundaries. Users can authenticate with secure browser sessions or scoped Personal API Tokens, while the system replays recoverable events and preserves evidence when recovery is impossible.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PostgreSQL unavailability blocks new Runs and returns a clear readiness/error contract without corrupting existing evidence.
- [ ] A bounded append-only Event Spool buffers and replays transient events; capacity exhaustion cancels the affected Run while preserving evidence and reports the reason.
- [ ] Worker scheduling avoids starvation from blocked Deployments, and lease conflicts produce waiting rather than infrastructure failure.
- [ ] Personal API Tokens are displayed once, stored hash-only, scoped to read/run/report, expiring, revocable, and rejected outside their scope.
- [ ] Admin, Operator, and Viewer permissions are enforced across Run, Artifact, debug-capture, judge, Sandbox, export, and management operations.
- [ ] Credential plaintext and protected judge/Sandbox content are absent from logs, snapshots, API responses, exports, and ordinary-user views.
- [ ] Reliability, outage recovery, Event Spool, scheduling, cancellation, token, and authorization integration tests pass.

## Blocked by

- #1736 — ticket: Compass identity models and deployments
- #1738 — ticket: Performance execution and telemetry metrics
- #1740 — ticket: Composite evaluations and suite scoring
- #1741 — ticket: Artifacts, comparisons, and exports

title: ticket: Artifacts, comparisons, and exports
body:
## Parent

#1734 — spec: AI Compute Compass V1

## What to build

Operators can inspect historical Performance and Composite Evaluation results, compare up to five compatible Runs, and export HTML, JSON, or CSV. Large, sensitive, and file-native content is retained through an authorized Artifact Store without exposing protected material.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A directory-backed Artifact Store abstraction uses stable storage keys and authenticated access rather than exposing absolute paths.
- [ ] EvalScope reports, complete predictions, logs, judge traces, Sandbox files, and other file-native outputs can be referenced as Artifacts while structured summaries remain in PostgreSQL.
- [ ] Full request, response, and stream bodies are not retained by default; Admin-authorized time-limited Debug Capture is bounded and protected.
- [ ] Soft-deleted Runs are hidden before asynchronous Artifact cleanup, and referenced versions cannot be hard-deleted.
- [ ] Run history and detail views show provenance, metrics, child results, and Artifact references with role-appropriate authorization.
- [ ] Comparison accepts at most five Runs and requires matching Comparison Signatures; incompatible Runs are clearly rejected.
- [ ] HTML, JSON, and CSV exports are available through API and user workflows without leaking credentials or protected judge/Sandbox content.
- [ ] Artifact retention, authorization, comparison, and export behavior has integration coverage.

## Blocked by

- #1738 — ticket: Performance execution and telemetry metrics
- #1740 — ticket: Composite evaluations and suite scoring

title: ticket: Composite evaluations and suite scoring
body:
## Parent

#1734 — spec: AI Compute Compass V1

## What to build

Operators can start a Composite Evaluation whose parent Run executes ordered independent Benchmark child processes, exposes completed child results immediately, preserves completed work on cancellation, and produces valid Ability Scores and a final Overall Score only when suite requirements are met.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Composite parent creates ordered Benchmark child Runs and executes them sequentially in independent CLI subprocesses.
- [ ] Child Attempts are immutable; failures require a manually created later Attempt and are never automatically retried.
- [ ] Parent progress is based on planned sample counts, child logs remain independently addressable, and merged logs are available.
- [ ] Cancellation preserves completed children and discards only the incomplete current attempt.
- [ ] Normalizers yield 0–100 contributions, explicit suite weights and Ability Mappings are applied, and provisional Ability Scores are available when valid contributors are ready.
- [ ] Missing required evidence is unavailable rather than zero or silently reweighted; Overall Score waits for parent completion and valid coverage using the default 95% Valid Sample Ratio.
- [ ] Candidate and Judge Deployments are separate, candidate self-judging is rejected, Judge Signatures are versioned, and coding evaluation uses an isolated Sandbox.
- [ ] Composite execution, scoring, coverage, cancellation, judge, and sandbox behavior has end-to-end and contract coverage.

## Blocked by

- #1738 — ticket: Performance execution and telemetry metrics
- #1739 — ticket: Benchmark catalog and evaluation suites

title: ticket: Benchmark catalog and evaluation suites
body:
## Parent

#1734 — spec: AI Compute Compass V1

## What to build

Admins can expose the local 22-dataset Benchmark Catalog, create immutable Dataset Revisions and Evaluation Suite Versions, and Operators can select Quick, Standard, or Full evaluation scales with exact manifests and ability mappings before submitting a run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The catalog is an allowlist of local read-only datasets and does not perform remote discovery.
- [ ] Dataset Revisions record immutable identity, file manifests, sizes, and checksum summaries.
- [ ] Suite versions bind benchmarks, evaluation versions, required/optional status, primary metrics, normalizers, explicit weights, Ability Mappings, prerequisites, execution settings, and exact Sample Manifests.
- [ ] Suite A includes aime24, aime25, aime26, gpqa_diamond, ifeval, math_500, and humaneval with the specified required core items.
- [ ] Quick, Standard, and Full scales use versioned seeded ordering and declared minimum stratum coverage.
- [ ] Catalog and Suite API/UI workflows and fixture-backed integration tests cover valid and invalid configurations.

## Blocked by

- #1735 — ticket: Compass run lifecycle and persistence
- #1736 — ticket: Compass identity models and deployments

title: ticket: Performance execution and telemetry metrics
body:
## Parent

#1734 — spec: AI Compute Compass V1

## What to build

Operators can start a Performance Run. A persistent Worker executes its Workload Plan through the EvalScope Adapter, a local Telemetry Proxy observes model traffic, and Compass presents live and final performance metrics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A queued Performance Run is selected by a Worker, acquires the required Deployment lease, and transitions through preparation, warmup, running, finalizing, and a terminal state.
- [ ] The EvalScope Adapter and Telemetry Proxy provide versioned contracts, with the Proxy as the canonical Compass metric source.
- [ ] Call Metrics, Session Metrics, one-second Live Metric Buckets, rolling P50/P95/P99, Actual QPS, Request/Token Throughput, Offered Load, Dropped Calls, and scheduling lag are persisted and queryable.
- [ ] Warmup observations are excluded; failed calls remain in success-rate denominators and are excluded from latency percentiles; non-streaming TTFT/TPOT are N/A.
- [ ] SSE live updates and REST recovery expose run state and metrics without retaining full traffic bodies by default.
- [ ] End-to-end API, Worker, Adapter, lease, telemetry, bucket, and metric contract tests pass.

## Blocked by

- #1737 — ticket: Versioned workload profiles and deterministic plans

title: ticket: Versioned workload profiles and deterministic plans
body:
## Parent

#1734 — spec: AI Compute Compass V1

## What to build

Admins can publish immutable Workload Profile Versions, and Operators can resolve a profile with public per-run overrides into a reproducible Workload Plan for Chat, RAG, Workflow, Tool Calling Simulation, Agent Simulation, and Coding Agent Simulation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Profile versions support Draft, Published, and Deprecated lifecycle semantics, with published versions immutable and deprecated versions available for history and cloning.
- [ ] Run creation records the selected profile version, public overrides, generated or cloned seed, and resolved Workload Plan provenance.
- [ ] The generator enforces V1 workload bounds, tokenizer-verified input budgets, target output budgets, shared prefixes, deterministic unique suffixes, supported context-growth strategies, and deployment selection rules.
- [ ] Chat/RAG support closed-loop concurrency and supported open-loop single-call load; multi-call workloads use closed-loop Virtual Sessions.
- [ ] Profile management and run-creation behavior are exposed through Compass APIs and the primary user workflow.
- [ ] Determinism, seed cloning, token budgets, and invalid-boundary cases have focused contract tests.

body:
## Parent

#1734 — spec: AI Compute Compass V1

## What to build

Admins can manage Models and Model Deployments, including capability declarations, capacity limits, availability, and encrypted credentials. Admin, Operator, and Viewer access is enforced through a basic server-side session boundary.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The first Admin can be bootstrapped through the deployment flow, and subsequent users can be assigned Admin, Operator, or Viewer roles.
- [ ] Models are separate from Deployments, and Deployment records include endpoint identity, declared capabilities, capacity limits, and availability state.
- [ ] Credentials are encrypted at rest and never appear in snapshots, logs, API responses, or structured results.

title: ticket: Compass run lifecycle and persistence
body:
## Parent

#1734 — spec: AI Compute Compass V1

## What to build

Compass can create, query, update, and soft-delete Test Runs; persist valid lifecycle transitions; and save one immutable Configuration Snapshot for each Run. The application exposes database readiness and a minimal run-detail workflow.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test Runs enforce the V1 kinds and lifecycle states, including valid timestamps and terminal-state behavior.
- [ ] Each Run can have exactly one immutable Configuration Snapshot containing resolved JSONB, source references, and a verified SHA-256 hash.
- [ ] Repository, service, and API operations support create, retrieve, lifecycle update, list, and soft delete while hiding deleted Runs from normal queries.
- [ ] Migrations are idempotent, protected by an advisory lock, and detect checksum drift.
- [ ] API and PostgreSQL integration tests cover persistence, constraints, snapshot immutability, readiness, and soft-delete visibility.

## Blocked by

- None — can start immediately.

title: spec: AI Compute Compass V1
body:
## Problem Statement

EvalScope already provides model evaluation and performance-test parameterization, but users lack one coherent, reproducible workflow for configuring workloads, executing runs, retaining structured results, and interpreting model capability. Compass must add this workflow without modifying EvalScope core behavior or importing historical `outputs/` data.

## Solution

Build AI Compute Compass V1 as an independently runnable application in the same repository. Compass is the primary user entry point; the original EvalScope UI remains available for advanced debugging. Compass resolves immutable Workload Profile and Evaluation Suite versions into immutable Configuration Snapshots, executes persistent Test Runs through a Benchmark Worker and versioned EvalScope Adapter, observes performance traffic through a local Telemetry Proxy, stores structured results in PostgreSQL, stores large or protected outputs in a directory-backed abstract Artifact Store, and exposes live/recoverable results through REST and SSE.

V1 provides Performance Runs and Composite Evaluations. Performance Runs generate deterministic synthetic workloads for Chat, RAG, Workflow, Tool Calling Simulation, Agent Simulation, and Coding Agent Simulation. Composite Evaluations execute the local read-only benchmark catalog as ordered independent child runs and aggregate valid normalized results into Ability Dimensions and, only when complete, a 0-100 Overall Score.

## User Stories

1. As an Operator, I want published Workload Profile parameters loaded into the detailed form, so that I can start consistent tests quickly.
2. As an Admin, I want profiles and Evaluation Suite versions immutable after publication, so that historical results remain reproducible.
3. As an Operator, I want per-run overrides recorded separately, so that experiments do not mutate shared defaults.
4. As an Operator, I want Chat and RAG workloads with concurrency or supported open-loop rate, token budgets, scenarios, and metric policies, so that common inference traffic can be measured.
5. As an Operator, I want Workflow stages, Tool Calling cycles, bounded Agent steps, and Coding Agent context growth, so that multi-call pressure can be simulated without real agents, tools, MCP, or business systems.
6. As an Operator, I want tokenizer-verified input budgets, target output budgets, shared prefixes, deterministic unique suffixes, and a recorded seed, so that workload plans are reproducible and token-accurate.
7. As an Operator, I want session-count or duration termination, warmup exclusion, and one Deployment per Virtual Session, so that test boundaries and endpoint identity are unambiguous.
8. As an Operator, I want Call Metrics, Session Metrics, one-second Live Metric Buckets, rolling P50/P95/P99, Actual QPS, Request Throughput, Token Throughput, Offered Load, Dropped Calls, and scheduling lag, so that overload and latency are not conflated.
9. As an Operator, I want streaming TTFT/TPOT when observable and N/A for non-streaming calls, so that unsupported precision is not implied.
10. As an Operator, I want all supported raw metrics collected while Metric Policy controls presentation, SLA interpretation, and recommendations, so that policy changes do not destroy observations.
11. As an Operator, I want persistent history, strict Comparison Signatures, comparison of up to five runs, and HTML/JSON/CSV export, so that results can be diagnosed and shared.
12. As an Admin, I want Model and Model Deployment separated, encrypted credentials, deployment limits, availability states, and leases, so that capacity and endpoint identity are controlled.
13. As an Admin, I want the initial Benchmark Catalog to be an allowlist of 22 local read-only datasets with immutable Dataset Revisions, so that evaluation does not depend on remote discovery.
14. As an Admin, I want Suite versions to bind benchmarks, evaluation versions, primary metrics, normalizers, weights, Ability Mappings, prerequisites, execution settings, and exact Sample Manifests, so that scoring cannot drift.
15. As an Operator, I want Quick, Standard, and Full scales and Suite A (`aime24`, `aime25`, `aime26`, `gpqa_diamond`, `ifeval`, `math_500`, `humaneval`), so that composite evaluation supports fast diagnosis and standard measurement.
16. As an Operator, I want a Composite parent Run with sequential independent Benchmark child processes, merged and separate logs, planned-sample progress, cancellation preservation, and manual later attempts, so that partial work and failures remain explainable.
17. As an Operator, I want Provisional Ability Scores while valid contributors finish but no Overall Score before parent completion, so that in-progress evidence is clearly provisional.
18. As an Operator, I want missing required evidence unavailable rather than zero or silently reweighted, with a default 95% Valid Sample Ratio, so that incomplete evidence is honest.
19. As an Admin, I want independent Judge Deployments and Judge Signatures plus isolated code execution, so that candidate self-judging and unsafe host execution are prohibited.
20. As an Operator, I want Compatibility Preflight to combine declared capabilities with a live probe and block mismatches before queueing, so that incompatible runs do not consume capacity.
21. As a Platform User, I want Admin, Operator, and Viewer roles, secure username/temporary-password login, server-side sessions, and scoped expiring hash-only Personal API Tokens, so that access is controlled.
22. As an Operator, I want SSE updates with REST recovery, PostgreSQL readiness gating, bounded Event Spool replay, and evidence-preserving failures, so that transient outages do not create silent data loss.
23. As an Admin, I want soft deletion before asynchronous Artifact cleanup and stable storage keys instead of absolute paths, so that retention and storage layout are controlled.
24. As a Compass maintainer, I want Adapter, EvalScope, evaluation, profile, suite, model, deployment, dataset, and judge versions recorded for every run, so that provenance is complete.
25. As a Compass maintainer, I want no historical `outputs/` import or Legacy Run view in V1, so that the new persistence model starts cleanly.

## Implementation Decisions

- Compass is independently runnable in the same repository and does not modify EvalScope core. Business workflows cross a versioned EvalScope Adapter boundary.
- V1 is single-node, multi-process. There is no scheduler, priority system, DAG/dependency orchestration, distributed queue, or automatic retry policy.
- A persistent Test Run owns lifecycle, immutable Configuration Snapshot, results, logs, and Artifact references. States are `queued`, `waiting_for_deployment`, `preparing`, `warming_up`, `running`, `cancelling`, `finalizing`, `completed`, `cancelled`, and `failed`. Model request failures remain measured outcomes; infrastructure/executor failure produces Failed.
- Workload Profile and Evaluation Suite versions are Admin-managed, organization-wide, and Draft/Published/Deprecated. Published versions create standard runs; deprecated versions remain usable for history and cloning.
- The Workload Generator resolves profile version, run overrides, and seed into a versioned Workload Plan. Chat/RAG support closed-loop and open-loop load; multi-call types use closed-loop Virtual Session concurrency. Synthetic waits affect Session Metrics only.
- New runs generate seeds; Clone reuses the seed; Clone to Deployment preserves the plan and changes only deployment. Strict comparison requires a matching versioned Comparison Signature.
- The local Telemetry Proxy is canonical for Compass performance metrics. It records bounded request/stream events without automatic model-call retries. EvalScope reports and logs are Audit Artifacts.
- PostgreSQL stores structured results. Each run captures one immutable snapshot containing resolved JSONB, queryable source/version references, and a content hash. Credential plaintext never enters snapshots, logs, responses, or results. Referenced versions cannot be hard-deleted; runs are soft-deleted before Artifact cleanup.
- Large, sensitive, or file-native content uses a directory-backed Artifact Store abstraction with stable keys and authenticated access. Full request/response/stream bodies are excluded by default; Admin-authorized, time-limited Debug Capture is supported.
- The initial catalog contains 22 local read-only datasets. Dataset Revisions are checksum-based. Suite A contains the seven named benchmarks; all core items are Required. Quick/Standard/Full are exact versioned Sample Manifests, with Quick 100-300 and Standard 1000-3000 default ranges and declared minimum strata coverage.
- A Composite Evaluation is a parent Run with ordered Benchmark children, sequential CLI subprocesses, independent attempts, immediate completed-child visibility, merged and child logs, and no automatic retries. Cancellation keeps completed children and discards only the incomplete attempt.
- Standard evaluations use locked suite scoring. Scoring-affecting customizations are detail-only and receive no standard Overall Score. Normalizers produce 0-100 contributions. Required missing evidence is unavailable, not zero; Overall Score appears only after parent completion and valid required coverage.
- Candidate and Judge Deployments are separate. Judge Signature versions model/prompt/output contract/generation/scoring code. Code-generation evaluation requires an isolated Sandbox. Compatibility Preflight is mandatory before queueing.
- Benchmark Worker selects the oldest runnable queued work without blocked-deployment starvation. Performance leases are exclusive; evaluation leases are bounded shared capacity and modes do not overlap. PostgreSQL outage blocks new runs; bounded Event Spool buffers/replays transient events and cancels on capacity exhaustion.
- Access is single-organization with Admin, Operator, and Viewer roles. Browser auth uses secure HttpOnly SameSite server-side sessions. Personal API Tokens are one-time displayed, expiring, revocable, hash-only, and scoped to read/run/report. V1 has no independent Audit Event subsystem.
- The highest testing seam is the Compass application/service/API. Tests verify external behavior through Compass APIs and run workflows. Focused tests cover deterministic Workload Generator behavior, Telemetry/metric contracts, scoring/normalization rules, Adapter contracts, and PostgreSQL semantics.

## Testing Decisions

- Assert external behavior through Compass API and run workflows, not private helper calls or internal layouts.
- API tests cover health/readiness, auth/roles, profile and suite resolution, run lifecycle, cancellation, clone/comparison, SSE/REST recovery, export, and Artifact authorization.
- PostgreSQL integration tests cover migrations, checksum drift, advisory-lock idempotence, state constraints, snapshot immutability, soft-delete visibility, leases, and structured results using isolated databases.
- Worker tests cover oldest-runnable selection, leases, cancellation, Event Spool replay/full behavior, benchmark ordering, manual attempts, and failure classification.
- Deterministic contract tests cover Workload Plan reproducibility/bounds, tokenizer budgets, comparison signatures, telemetry conversion, percentile/bucket semantics, score normalization, coverage gates, preflight, Sandbox requirements, and Adapter command/result contracts.
- Evaluation tests use local fixtures/read-only datasets, exact manifests, independent scripted judges, malformed/prose/transport failures, valid-ratio handling, isolated code execution, and rejection of candidate self-judging.
- Frontend end-to-end tests cover profile loading, run creation/cancellation, live/recovered state, intermediate child results, capability visualization, comparison, and export with external models/services mocked.
- Existing prior art is the Compass Flask test client and configuration-hash tests, plus EvalScope CLI, benchmark adapter, service, and judge contract tests.

## Out of Scope

- Historical `outputs/` or SQLite migration/import/display; remote dataset discovery; arbitrary benchmark directories.
- Changes to EvalScope core evaluator, registries, model APIs, benchmark adapters, or original UI.
- Real Agent/tool/MCP/business-system execution, tool correctness validation, workflow automation, deployment launch/shutdown/autoscaling.
- Scheduler, priorities, DAGs, distributed queue, multi-node execution, horizontal coordination, automatic retries, and open-loop multi-call workloads.
- Default full content retention, candidate self-judging, non-isolated code execution, universal cross-suite ranking, Overall Score for incomplete/custom scoring runs, independent Audit Events, external SSO, self-registration, multi-organization tenancy, and mobile-native clients.

## Further Notes

The existing Compass persistence foundation must be extended rather than duplicated: migration runner with advisory locking and checksum drift detection, initial Run and immutable Snapshot tables, configuration hashing, repository ports, and health/readiness endpoints already exist. Dedicated Compass PostgreSQL role/database and Compass-specific MCP configuration are implementation prerequisites; existing services and connections must remain untouched, and secrets must never enter source control, issue bodies, logs, or API responses.

title: Add AgentX workload support to EvalScope Perf
Report list: group same-model reports for display, without merging report directories
body:
### Context

Our eval workflow runs one model against datasets incrementally—often as separate invocations (different dataset, different day) rather than one big run. The report list therefore ends up with N rows per model. For example, a model evaluated on 6 datasets across 3 separate runs appears as 3 unrelated rows, with no way to see the model's full picture without opening each report individually.

We tried solving this by physically merging report directories in #1570. @Yunnglin correctly closed it:

> I'm closing this because the feature mutates/deletes source evaluation runs, which conflicts with EvalScope treating reports as immutable audit records. The merged `task_config.yaml` only keeps the first source run's config, so the report claims one setup produced scores that came from different settings; logs and `collection_detailed_report.json` are also dropped. The underlying need—seeing one model across multiple datasets—is better solved in the viewer layer, and the framework already supports it: resuming an existing run with an extended dataset list via `use_cache` writes everything into one directory with honest provenance.
>
> Could you open an issue describing the original scenario instead?

This is that issue, along with a working alternative.

### Going forward vs. already-split history

For *new* runs, `use_cache` + an extended `datasets` list already does the right thing (confirmed).

However, this doesn't help with runs that are already split across directories, nor does it provide a fast way to see cross-dataset coverage per model in the list UI generally. Using `use_cache` in this case would mean re-evaluating every dataset that isn't already present in whichever single directory you resume from, since `use_cache`'s cache lookup is scoped to one `work_dir`.

### Proposed / implemented: view-layer grouping, no file mutation

We put together a display-only alternative and would like feedback before opening a PR:

* `GET /api/v1/reports?group_by=model` rolls same-model report-list items into one row each, entirely in memory, using metadata the endpoint already loads for the flat list (`_build_report_meta` results grouped by `model_name`). No report is read, written, moved, or merged.
* Each group carries `children`: every constituent report exactly as the flat list describes it, with its own `run_id`, `model_id`, and `primary_metrics`. This means a group never shows a fabricated combined score.
* If a dataset appears in more than one of the model's reports, there is no silent "winner"; both remain visible under their respective reports when the group is expanded.
* The report list UI adds a **Group by model** toggle that renders these as expandable rows, reusing the existing `ReportsTable` / `ReportCard` components for the expanded children, so no new row-rendering logic is needed.
* The group's **Compare all** action reuses the existing multi-report Compare flow (`report=` query params), which is already used by `/api/v1/reports/charts/<type>`.

We have this working end-to-end against a real multi-run output directory, with backend and frontend tests passing and `tsc` / `eslint` clean.

Happy to open a PR, reusing the `SelectionTray` / list UI pieces from #1570 where relevant. We wanted to confirm first that the shape of `group_by=model`—including the field names and duplicate-dataset display—is agreeable, per your comment on #1570.

title: External agent bridge drops perf_metrics (and reasoning) from the transcript, so collect_perf records nothing for bridge runs
body:
## Self-Check List

- [x] I have carefully read the [relevant user documentation](https://evalscope.readthedocs.io/en/latest/get_started/parameters.html)
- [x] I have reviewed the [Frequently Asked Questions](https://evalscope.readthedocs.io/en/latest/get_started/faq.html)
- [x] I have searched and reviewed existing issues to confirm this is not a duplicate problem

## Problem Description

In External Agent Bridge mode, the transcript the bridge reconstructs drops `perf_metrics` from every assistant message. `DefaultEvaluator._record_perf` reads `perf_metrics` off exactly those messages (`evaluator/evaluator.py:424-441`, falling back to `task_state.output.perf_metrics`, which the bridge adapter also builds from plain text). So with `collect_perf=True`, which is the default, an external-agent evaluation ends with an empty perf table and `coverage.requests_with_metrics = 0`, although the bridge measured `latency_ms` for every call and the upstream `ModelAPI` attached `PerformanceMetrics` to the output.

The same rebuild also throws away the reasoning blocks and the `model` id, so the trace view of a bridge run cannot show what the model was thinking.

Root cause: `BridgeTraceRecorder._build_assistant_message` (`agent/external/bridge/trace_recorder.py`) creates a fresh `ChatMessageAssistant(content=src.text, tool_calls=...)` instead of copying `output.message`. The native loop snapshots the message with `output.message.model_copy(deep=True)` (`AgentLoop._snapshot_assistant_message`), and the recorder's module docstring says both paths should produce the same trace shape.

## EvalScope Version (Required)

`main` @ `c31f0f9` (dev install). The rebuild has been in `trace_recorder.py` since at least `3791993`, so v1.11.1 should behave the same (not verified on the release wheel).

## Tools Used
- [x] Native / Native framework
- [ ] Opencompass backend
- [ ] VLMEvalKit backend
- [ ] RAGEval backend
- [ ] Perf / Model inference stress testing tool
- [ ] Arena / Arena mode

## Executed Code or Instructions

Zero external dependencies: `MockLLM` as the backend and the bundled `mock` runner in a `local` environment.

```python
from evalscope.agent.external import ExternalAgentConfig
from evalscope.agent.external.adapter import run_external_agent
from evalscope.agent.external.bridge.trace_recorder import BridgeTraceRecorder
from evalscope.api.dataset import Sample
from evalscope.api.messages import ChatMessageAssistant, ContentReasoning, ContentText
from evalscope.api.messages.perf_metrics import PerformanceMetrics
from evalscope.api.model import GenerateConfig, Model, ModelOutput
from evalscope.api.model.model_output import ChatCompletionChoice
from evalscope.models.mockllm import MockLLM
from evalscope.utils.asyncio_runtime import AsyncioLoopRunner

def make_output() -> ModelOutput:
    msg = ChatMessageAssistant(content=[ContentReasoning(reasoning='6*7 is 42'), ContentText(text='42')])
    msg.perf_metrics = PerformanceMetrics(latency=0.123, ttft=0.05, input_tokens=10, output_tokens=2)
    return ModelOutput(model='mock-model', choices=[ChatCompletionChoice(message=msg, stop_reason='stop')])

# 1. recorder level
rec = BridgeTraceRecorder(trial_id='t', framework='mock')
rec.record_anthropic_turn({'messages': [{'role': 'user', 'content': 'q'}]}, make_output(), latency_ms=123.0)
a = [m for m in rec.messages() if m.role == 'assistant'][0]
print('perf on recorded assistant msg:', a.perf_metrics)
print('content type:', type(a.content).__name__)

# 2. end to end through the bridge
model = Model(api=MockLLM(model_name='mock-model', custom_outputs=[make_output()]), config=GenerateConfig())
res = run_external_agent(ExternalAgentConfig(framework='mock', environment='local', timeout=60), model, Sample(input='what is 6*7?', id=1))
assistants = [m for m in res.messages if m.role == 'assistant']
print('perf on transcript:', [m.perf_metrics for m in assistants])
print('perf on output:', res.output.perf_metrics)
perfs = [m.perf_metrics for m in assistants if m.perf_metrics is not None] or ([res.output.perf_metrics] if res.output.perf_metrics else [])
print('requests_with_metrics _record_perf would count:', len(perfs), 'of', len(assistants))
AsyncioLoopRunner.shutdown_for_thread()
```

## Error Log

No exception; the data is silently missing.

```
perf on recorded assistant msg: None
content type: str                      <- reasoning block dropped as well
perf on transcript: [None]
perf on output: None
requests_with_metrics _record_perf would count: 0 of 1
```

The bridge log for the same call shows it did measure the turn: `bridge[mock/…] step=0 json latency=0.00s tokens=0+0 stop='stop'`, and the `MODEL_GENERATE` trace event carries `latency_ms=123.0`.

For comparison, a native `AgentLoop` run with the same `MockLLM` keeps `perf_metrics` on the assistant message (the loop deep-copies `output.message`).

## Running Environment

- Operating System: macOS 15 (Darwin 24.6.0)
- Python Version: 3.12.12

## Additional Information

Suggested fix: make `_build_assistant_message` return `src.model_copy(deep=True, update={'tool_calls': normalised_tool_calls})`, keeping only the existing `tool_calls` normalisation (`unpack_tool_call` exists because some upstream paths leave `ToolCall.function` as a bare string). That restores `perf_metrics`, reasoning, `model` and `metadata` in one step and matches what the native loop does. I have a PR with this change plus recorder-level and end-to-end tests ready and will link it here.

Related: #1698 (upstream failures were also missing from bridge traces); this is the same theme of the bridge transcript carrying less than the native one.

Follow-up to #1578: judge prompt placeholder injection ({gold} splice); unseeded bootstrap CI bounds; metric crash recorded as zero with SUCCESS status; allow_inclusion grades by substring
body:
## Summary

Four defects at pin 3c52bd0 (extends #1578, which was fixed in #1588).

### 1. Judge prompt placeholder injection

Sequential str.replace over the whole prompt means a model answer containing the literal `{gold}` splices the reference answer into the predicted-answer section. A wrong answer scores 1.0.

### 2. Unseeded bootstrap confidence bounds

The arena bootstrap resamples with no seed; three fresh-process runs on identical battles produce different 97.5 percent bounds (0.6875, 0.7203, 0.7828).

### 3. Metric crash recorded as zero with SUCCESS status

The adapter's except-handler writes value=0 and keeps the default SUCCESS status, so a crashing metric plugin counts as a wrong answer in the mean denominator, contradicting the project's own ScoreStatus contract.

### 4. Accuracy with allow_inclusion grades by Python `in`

A list reference gives full credit for one-of-several required letters while the complete answer scores zero; alias lists become exact-match case-sensitive; string references become substring.

All four reproduce with deterministic offline stubs. Available as PRs with tests.

title: MCP over HTTP transport always fails with CancelledError; stdio unusable in service mode
body:
## Summary

`agent_config.mcp_servers` with `type: "http"` never works: every sample fails with
`concurrent.futures._base.CancelledError` before any tool call is made. The *same*
config with `type: "stdio"` works fine.

Separately, `stdio` transport does not work under `evalscope service`, so in service
mode **neither** MCP transport is usable.

## Reproduction

Only needs `mock_llm` — no real model or third-party API required.

```bash
PY=python  # your evalscope env

# A) stdio  -> succeeds
$PY -m evalscope.cli.cli eval \
  --model mock --eval-type mock_llm \
  --datasets deepsearchqa --limit 1 \
  --judge '{"strategy":"rule"}' \
  --agent-config '{"mode":"native","tools":["submit"],"mcp_servers":[
      {"type":"stdio","name":"fetch","command":"'"$PY"'","args":["-m","mcp_server_fetch"]}]}' \
  --work-dir ./repro_stdio

# B) http  -> every sample fails with CancelledError
#    (point the url at any StreamableHTTP MCP server)
$PY -m evalscope.cli.cli eval \
  --model mock --eval-type mock_llm \
  --datasets deepsearchqa --limit 1 \
  --judge '{"strategy":"rule"}' \
  --agent-config '{"mode":"native","tools":["submit"],"mcp_servers":[
      {"type":"http","name":"x","url":"http://127.0.0.1:9199/mcp","timeout":120}]}' \
  --work-dir ./repro_http
```

A ends with `Finished evaluation for mock on ['deepsearchqa']`.
B ends with `score computed from 0/1 successful samples; 1 errored`.

## Traceback (case B)

```
File "evalscope/api/benchmark/adapters/agent_adapter.py", line 248, in _on_inference
    result: AgentLoopResult = run_agent_loop(
File "evalscope/api/agent/runner.py", line 121, in run_agent_loop
    return AsyncioLoopRunner.run(_run())
File "evalscope/utils/asyncio_runtime.py", line 340, in run
    return handle.run_sync(coro, timeout=timeout)
File "evalscope/utils/asyncio_runtime.py", line 222, in run_sync
    return future.result(timeout=timeout)
concurrent.futures._base.CancelledError
```

Note it is `CancelledError`, not `TimeoutError` — the future is already cancelled when
`result()` is called, i.e. the coroutine never got to run on the owned loop. My guess is
that the MCP SDK's `AsyncExitStack` / anyio task-group lifecycle conflicts with the
generation lifecycle of `AsyncioLoopRunner`, but I have not isolated it further.

Failure is immediate (all log lines share the same second) and the MCP server receives
no requests at all, so the connection is never established.

`stateless=True` vs `stateless=False` on the server side makes no difference. Concurrency
makes no difference either (`--eval-batch-size 1` and `48` both fail).

## Second, related problem: stdio does not work under `evalscope service`

Submitting the stdio variant through `POST /api/v1/eval/invoke` fails with:

```
File "asyncio/unix_events.py", line 818, in _start
    self._proc = subprocess.Popen(
File "subprocess.py", line 1745, in _get_handles
    errwrite = stderr.fileno()
io.UnsupportedOperation: fileno
```

The evaluation runs in a `multiprocessing.spawn` child of the Flask service, where
`sys.stderr` has been replaced by a non-file logging object, so `stdio_client` cannot
spawn the MCP server process.

Combined with the HTTP issue above, this means **MCP tools cannot be used at all in
service mode** — only `CLI + stdio` works.

## Environment

- evalscope 1.11.1 (also reproduced the HTTP issue on the CLI path, so not service-specific)
- mcp 1.29.1
- Python 3.11.15, Linux

## Impact / why this may have gone unnoticed

No built-in benchmark uses `agent_config.mcp_servers`: `mcp_atlas` talks to its own
gateway with plain synchronous `requests` (`/enabled-servers`, `/list-tools`,
`/call-tool`), and other agentic benchmarks provide tools via `build_tools()`. So this
only affects users attaching their own external MCP tools — which is exactly what the
DeepSearchQA adapter docstring recommends:

> To evaluate a web-capable agent, set `TaskConfig.agent_config` and attach the
> search/fetch tools that should be available to the model.

Happy to test a patch.

title: [Bug] evalscope 1.11.1 perf TTFT statistics anomalous and abnormally high (min/P1/P5/P10/P25 all 0, P50 jumps to ~9555ms)
body:
## Description

After upgrading to `evalscope 1.11.1`, the TTFT (time-to-first-token) statistics reported by `evalscope perf` are anomalous and **abnormally high**:

- All lower percentiles (`min` / `P1` / `P5` / `P10` / `P25`) are reported as **0 ms**
- The value suddenly jumps to ~9555 ms at `P50` (real TTFT for this setup is a few hundred ms)
- Overall TTFT numbers are inflated / statistically distorted

Running the exact same command on `1.11.0` reports correct, monotonically increasing percentiles.

## Environment

- evalscope: **1.11.1** (buggy) vs **1.11.0** (correct)
- Target service: vLLM OpenAI-compatible API (`/v1/chat/completions`)
- OS: Linux x86_64, running inside a Python virtualenv

## Repro

```bash
evalscope perf \
  --api openai \
  --model <model> \
  --url <vllm_url>/v1/chat/completions \
  --dataset random \
  --prefix-length 0 \
  --min-prompt-length 1024 \
  --max-prompt-length 1024 \
  --max-tokens 1024 \
  --parallel 8 \
  --number 40 \
  --tokenizer-path <tokenizer_path> \
  --extra-args '{"ignore_eos": true}'
```

## Expected

TTFT percentiles increase monotonically from `min` to `P100`; `min`/`P1` should reflect the fastest real request (hundreds of ms in this setup).

## Actual (1.11.1)

```
TTFT percentile table:
  min:  0
  P1:   0
  P5:   0
  P10:  0
  P25:  0
  P50:  ~9555  (sudden jump, abnormally high)
  ...
```

- Every request succeeded (`40/40`) with a valid measured TTFT, yet lower percentiles are all 0 and the curve is distorted/high.
- Same anomaly reproduces at other concurrency settings, not specific to `parallel=8`.

## Notes

- Looks like a regression in the TTFT latency aggregation / percentile computation introduced between 1.11.0 and 1.11.1.
- Rolling back with `pip install evalscope==1.11.0` resolves the issue with identical command/config.

Screenshot of the observed percentile table attached (in original report).

title: AgentLoop docstrings point at AgentTrace.final_prediction, which does not exist
body:
## Summary

Three docstrings describe the reported prediction as living in `AgentTrace.final_prediction`. `AgentTrace` has no such field, and nothing in the repo ever sets it.

## Where

**`evalscope/api/agent/loop.py:363`** — `AgentLoop._emit_submit`

> ``final_answer`` here is what the *loop observed*, not the prediction that gets reported: that is resolved after the loop returns and lives in ``AgentTrace.final_prediction``.

**`evalscope/api/agent/loop.py:384`** — `AgentLoop._emit_implicit_submit`

> Only a short preview is kept, for diagnosis; the reported prediction is ``AgentTrace.final_prediction``.

**`tests/agent/test_native_runner.py:272`** — `test_run_native_agent_reports_the_adapter_resolved_prediction`

> ``trace.final_prediction`` is recorded further downstream, at the single point every inference path converges (``DefaultDataAdapter.run_inference``), not here [...]

## Why I believe this is stale rather than something I'm missing

1. `AgentTrace` (`evalscope/api/agent/trace.py:87`) declares only `framework`, `strategy`, `environment`, `max_steps`, `trial_id`, `total_usage`, `events`.
2. It declares no `model_config`, so under pydantic v2 the attribute cannot be assigned dynamically either.
3. `grep -rn "final_prediction" evalscope/ tests/` returns exactly those three comments — no definition, no assignment anywhere in the repo.

## Why it matters

`_emit_submit`'s docstring exists specifically to stop a reader conflating *what the loop observed* with *what actually gets scored* — a distinction that matters for adapters like SWE-bench that resolve their own artifact out of the trajectory. Following the pointer leads nowhere, so the warning loses its second half exactly where a new adapter author needs it.

As far as I can tell the resolution actually happens in `AgentAdapter._on_inference` via `_extract_final_answer`, landing in `InferenceResult.output.completion` (`evalscope/api/benchmark/adapters/agent_adapter.py:269-273`), and `DefaultDataAdapter.run_inference` is indeed the convergence point the test docstring describes.

## Question

Was `final_prediction` removed, or is it planned but not yet implemented?

- **Removed** → I've opened a comments-only PR repointing the three references at `_extract_final_answer`.
- **Planned** → the comments are right and the missing field is the real gap; happy to help there instead, and I'll close the PR.

One note either way: the test docstring records genuinely useful history (*"an earlier revision wrote it in this runner and consequently left it unset for every adapter that assembles its own `InferenceResult` (SWE-bench among them)"*). I kept that paragraph and only corrected the reference — it seems worth preserving.

## Summary

#1629 proposes the migration to `ruff`. This issue document possible improvements that enhances the CICD workflow (mostly `pre-commit`).

Since CICD causes a lot of file updates, I will leave all changes to maintainers and only propose ways to improve. (I found issue > PR, due to a lot of conflicts and merges.)

## Linting

- [x] I ([isort](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/#isort-i))
- [x] E ([pydocstyle error](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/#pycodestyle-e-w))
- [x] W ([pydocstyle warning](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/#pycodestyle-e-w))
- [x] ~~B ([flake8-bugbear](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/#flake8-bugbear-b))~~
- [x] ~~Q ([flake8-quotes](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/#flake8-quotes-q))~~
- [ ] UP ([pyupgrade](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/#pyupgrade-up))
- [ ] SIM ([flake8-simplify](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/#flake8-simplify-sim))
- [x] remove flake8 from pre-commit hook
- [ ] F401 in `evalscope`
- [ ] E/F/W rules in `tests`

## Formatting

- [x] add ruff-format and remove yapf in pre-commit hook (example: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/26247)

## Why do we need migration?

In addition to discussion #1629, ruff brings a faster, unified lint+format experience, as flake8 and yapf may conflict, an example:

```py
match var:
    # some comments here
    case 1:
        pass
```

flake8 will always format as above, while yapf will always format as below. This makes `make lint` never pass.

```py
match var:
# some comments here
    case 1:
        pass
```

title: One transient gateway error aborts the whole run: choices=None raised outside the retry boundary
body:
## Self-Check List

- [x] I have carefully read the [relevant user documentation](https://evalscope.readthedocs.io/en/latest/get_started/parameters.html)
- [x] I have reviewed the [Frequently Asked Questions](https://evalscope.readthedocs.io/en/latest/get_started/faq.html) — it does not cover this error
- [x] I have searched and reviewed existing issues to confirm this is not a duplicate problem

## Problem Description

While running GSM8K against the free-tier model `minimax/minimax-m3:free` on OpenRouter, some requests came back with `200 OK` — but the body wasn't a completion at all. It was an error saying the account balance had run out:

```json
{"error":{"message":"Insufficient balance","code":402}}
```

The OpenAI SDK parses that into a `ChatCompletion` with `choices=None`, so to everything downstream it still looks like a successful call.

**The response is checked in the wrong place.** [`retry_call`](https://github.com/modelscope/evalscope/blob/3c52bd0923b75b2a83b776d6f526feb70572bfdf/evalscope/models/openai_compatible.py#L156-L161) only covers the HTTP call, and nothing raises there — the request *succeeded*. The failure only surfaces later at [line 169](https://github.com/modelscope/evalscope/blob/3c52bd0923b75b2a83b776d6f526feb70572bfdf/evalscope/models/openai_compatible.py#L169), inside [`chat_choices_from_openai`](https://github.com/modelscope/evalscope/blob/3c52bd0923b75b2a83b776d6f526feb70572bfdf/evalscope/models/utils/openai.py#L673-L679), which is outside the retry block.

So `retries=5` can never apply, and with the default `ignore_errors=False` one bad response ends the whole run. Mine died at sample 44 of 1319.

The error message is also unhelpful — the real reason survives in `model_extra`, but nothing reads it, so you only see `id=None, model=None`.

## EvalScope Version (Required)

v1.11.0 (also reproduced on `main` @ `3c52bd0`)

## Tools Used

- [x] Native / Native framework

## Executed Code or Instructions

```python
import os
from evalscope import TaskConfig, run_task

OR_KEY = os.getenv("OPENROUTER_API_KEY")
OR_BASE = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1"

MODEL = 'minimax/minimax-m3:free'

task_cfg = TaskConfig(
    model=MODEL,
    api_url=OR_BASE,
    api_key=OR_KEY,
    eval_type="openai_api",

    datasets=["gsm8k"],

    # limit=5,                  # quick sanity check
    eval_batch_size=5,

    generation_config={
        "temperature": 0,
        "max_tokens": 1024,
    },

    dataset_args={
        "gsm8k": {
            "few_shot_num": 0,
            "few_shot_random": False,
        }
    }
)

run_task(task_cfg)
```

It depends on the upstream provider failing mid-run, so it won't reproduce on every attempt. It happened at sample 44 of one run, and three times during a later 200-sample run.

## Error Log

```
Evaluating[gsm8k]:   3%|██▉  | 44/1319 [00:55<24:59,  1.18s/it]
ERROR: Model [minimax/minimax-m3:free] returned an invalid response: Model response
contains no choices (choices=None). Response id=None, model=None. This may indicate
the model returned an empty or malformed response.

  File "evalscope/evaluator/evaluator.py", line 515, in _predict_sample
    task_state = self.benchmark.run_inference(model=self.model, sample=sample, ...)
  File "evalscope/api/benchmark/adapters/default_data_adapter.py", line 437, in _on_inference
    model_output = model.generate(input=sample.input, tools=sample.tools)
  File "evalscope/models/openai_compatible.py", line 145, in generate
    choices = self.chat_choices_from_completion(completion, tools)
  File "evalscope/models/utils/openai.py", line 666, in chat_choices_from_openai
    raise ValueError(
ValueError: Model response contains no choices (choices=None). Response id=None,
model=None. This may indicate the model returned an empty or malformed response.
```

## Running Environment

- Operating System: Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2
- Python Version: 3.12.3

## Additional Information

Fix in #1673: check the response where it comes back and raise a clear error if the body carries one, so the retry can act on it and the gateway's real message is reported. Only the `choices=None` case changes; real HTTP errors are untouched.

Workaround until then: set `ignore_errors=True`, which costs the affected sample instead of the run.

title: (bug) IFEval 中的 inst_level_* 实际用的是 macro-average，而不是官方的 micro-average
body:
## 自查清单

在提交 issue 之前，请确保您已完成以下步骤:
- [x] 我已仔细阅读了[相关使用说明文档](https://evalscope.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/get_started/parameters.html)
- [x] 我已查看了[常见问题解答](https://evalscope.readthedocs.io/zh-cn/latest/get_started/faq.html)
- [x] 我已搜索并查看了现有的 issues，确认这不是一个重复的问题

## 问题描述

IFEval 中的 inst_level_*  实际用的是 macro-average，而不是官方的 micro-average 
用 Qwen3-1.7B 跑 IFEval 的时候，发现 `inst_level_strict` 指标对不上，但 `prompt_level_strict` 没问题。
发现是指标计算问题，让cc扫了一下，发现影响范围还挺大的。

### micro-average 应该的实现
 `evalscope/benchmarks/ifbench/evaluation_lib.py`的中`print_report`的实现是把整个数据集的指令拉平，最后只除一次：

```python
instruction_total   += len(instruction_id_list)
instruction_correct += sum(follow_instruction_list)
...
print(f"instruction-level: {instruction_correct / instruction_total}")
```

即 **micro-average**，权重落在单条指令上：含 3 条指令的 prompt 对最终分数的贡献是含 1 条指令 prompt 的 3 倍。

### 实际实现

等价于的 **macro-average**：

1. `evalscope/benchmarks/ifeval/utils.py:131-133` — `agg_inst_level_acc` 在**单样本内**先做 `sum(items) / len(items)`，把该样本的指令池压成一个 [0,1] 比率；
2. `evalscope/benchmarks/ifeval/utils.py:125,127` — 该比率作为 `inst_level_strict` / `inst_level_loose` 写入 `Score.value`（`ifeval_adapter.py:106-107`）；
3. `evalscope/api/benchmark/meta.py:92` — 默认 `aggregation: str = 'mean'`，`IFEvalAdapter` 的 `BenchmarkMeta` 未覆盖；
4. `evalscope/metrics/aggregators/aggregators.py:76-93` — `Mean` 对每个 metric 无条件 `append(value)` 后 `mean(values)`，无任何权重。

一条指令的样本和三条指令的样本在最终分数里权重完全相同。

### 扫出来的影响范围

共三处：

| benchmark | 链路 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `ifeval` | `ifeval_adapter.py:106-107` → `ifeval/utils.py:131` | 如上 |
| `ifbench` | `ifbench_adapter.py:82,93` → `ifbench/evaluation_lib.py` 的 `process_results` | 复用同名函数，同样的 `agg_inst_level_acc` 两级归约 |
| `multi_if` | `multi_if_adapter.py:176-177` → `multi_if/metrics.py:100-105` | 调用 `parse_result([outputs_strict])` 传入**单元素 list**，micro 逻辑在 n=1 时退化为单样本比率，再交给 `Mean` 宏平均 |

**扫出来的次生问题**：三个 adapter 在 checker 抛异常时都走 `score.value = {}`（如 `ifeval_adapter.py:112-115`），而 `Mean` 只对存在该 key 的样本累加，所以分母会静默缩小、不留痕迹。#1606 里已经出现过 `Error calculating ifbench metrics`（NLTK 资源缺失）导致样本被跳过的实例。在 micro 语义下这类跳过对分数的影响更直接，建议一并考虑是否要显式上报被跳过的样本数。

### 如果确定这个是问题而不是期望的实现，我提个PR把这个改掉
但目前看由于前注册的聚合器只有 `mean`、`clipped_mean` 和三个 pass/vote@k（`aggregators.py`），没有加权均值，改这个需要动框架

## EvalScope 版本（必填）
v1.11.0

## 使用的工具
- [x] Native / 原生框架

## 运行环境

- 操作系统：
- Python版本：3.14

如果有其他相关信息，请在此处提供。

title: [Bug]: IFBench ratio:sentence_words accepts repeated words
body:
## Self-Check List

- [x] I have reviewed the relevant documentation and existing issues.
- [x] I confirmed this is not covered by an open or closed PR.

## Problem Description

`CharacterCountUniqueWordsChecker` describes the constraint as: "Respond with three sentences, all containing the same number of characters but using all different words." However, `check_following()` validates only the sentence count and equal character lengths. It never checks word uniqueness.

This creates deterministic false positives in IFBench strict and loose scores. For example, `Cat. Cat. Cat.` has three equal-length sentences and is currently accepted even though every word is repeated.

## Minimal Reproduction

```python
from evalscope.benchmarks.ifbench.instructions import CharacterCountUniqueWordsChecker

checker = CharacterCountUniqueWordsChecker("ratio:sentence_words")
assert checker.check_following("Cat. Cat. Cat.") is True  # current behavior
```

## Expected Behavior

The checker should reject a response when any case-insensitive word token is repeated across the three sentences, while preserving the existing sentence-count and character-count checks. Standalone punctuation tokens should not participate in uniqueness.

## Proposed Fix

Reuse the existing `_word_tokens_without_punctuation()` helper, normalize tokens with `casefold()`, and require the token count to equal the unique-token count. Add focused offline tests for repeated words, case-insensitive duplicates, punctuation, unequal sentence lengths, and a valid response.

## EvalScope Version

Current `main` at the time of filing.

## Tools Used

- [x] Native / Native framework

title: litellm imports are nested inside functions for a reason that no longer holds
body:
## What I noticed

`evalscope/models/litellm_compatible.py` imports litellm inside `generate()`, inside `generate_async()`, and inside `_litellm_no_retry_exceptions()`. The helper's docstring gives the reason:

> The litellm import stays lazy to keep this module importable without litellm.

That isn't true in this repo.

**litellm is a base dependency, not an extra.** It's in `requirements/framework.txt`, which `pyproject.toml` maps straight to `dependencies`:

```toml
[tool.setuptools.dynamic]
dependencies = {file = ["requirements/framework.txt"]}
```

So it installs with a plain `pip install evalscope`. There is no supported setup where this module exists but litellm doesn't.

**The registry already gates it anyway**, one layer up in `evalscope/models/model_apis.py`:

```python
@register_model_api(name='litellm')
def litellm_api() -> type[ModelAPI]:
    check_import('litellm', package='litellm', raise_error=True, feature_name='litellm')

    from .litellm_compatible import LiteLLMAPI
```

`check_import(..., raise_error=True)` runs *before* the module is imported. By the time the module body executes, litellm is guaranteed importable — and a missing litellm still gets the same clean, feature-named error instead of an `ImportError` surfacing from inside `generate()` mid-run.

## The neighbouring provider already does it the other way

`anthropic_compatible.py` imports its SDK at module level:

```python
from anthropic import (Anthropic, APIStatusError, AsyncAnthropic, ...)
```

And `anthropic` is a *harder* case than litellm — it isn't in any requirements file at all, so it's fully optional, install-your-own. It relies on the same `check_import` gate in `model_apis.py` and that works fine.

So the mandatory dependency is being treated more defensively than the fully optional one. It's backwards.

## What about import cost?

`import litellm` is genuinely slow — I measured **2.086 s**. That would be a good reason to defer it, except the registry already does: this module isn't imported at all unless someone selects `eval_type='litellm'`. The laziness is already at the right layer, so hoisting adds nothing to startup.

For completeness, calling `_litellm_no_retry_exceptions()` per request costs **0.152 µs**, which is nothing against multi-second requests. This is a readability issue, not a performance one.

## Suggested change

With the laziness redundant, the helper can be a module constant — which is how the sibling module states the same thing:

```python
# openai_compatible.py
NON_RETRYABLE_OPENAI_ERRORS: Tuple[Type[Exception], ...] = (...)
```

So:

```python
import litellm
from litellm.exceptions import (
    AuthenticationError, BadRequestError, NotFoundError,
    PermissionDeniedError, UnprocessableEntityError,
)

NON_RETRYABLE_LITELLM_ERRORS: Tuple[Type[Exception], ...] = (
    AuthenticationError, BadRequestError, NotFoundError,
    PermissionDeniedError, UnprocessableEntityError,
)
```

No behaviour change — same five exception types, both call sites pass the constant unchanged.

## Scope

I checked whether this pattern is widespread before proposing anything. It is: there are ~93 nested imports of base dependencies across the codebase. Most are defensible — deferring something heavy like `pandas`, `transformers`, `PIL` or `plotly` inside a module that *is* imported eagerly genuinely saves startup time.

`evalscope/models/` is different. It has only three other nested third-party imports:

- `modelscope.py:169` — `StopStringCriteria` inside an `if config.stop_seqs is not None:` branch. A conditional, rarely-taken path; fine as is.
- `utils/anthropic.py:697,867` — `anthropic` inside the stream collectors.

So this isn't a call to change the convention everywhere. It's one module where the stated reason doesn't hold, the module is already deferred, and the sibling provider does it the other way.

I've deliberately kept this PR to that single file so it stays easy to review. The same thing does show up in a few other places — the two `utils/anthropic.py` sites above being the closest — and I'm happy to raise a follow-up PR for those if you agree with the direction here. Equally happy to leave the convention alone if you'd rather; just let me know which you'd prefer.

## Verification

`pytest tests/models/` → 92 passed. `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean. No remaining references to the removed helper.

title: perf(multi-turn): warmup still drains before the measured window, and benchmark conversations pay a cold first turn
body:
## Problem

`MultiTurnStrategy.run()` still runs warmup as a separate phase that completes in full before any benchmark conversation starts:

```python
# Two-phase dispatch: warmup conversations complete in full before any
# benchmark conversation starts.  ``_conv_index`` persists across
# phases so warmup and benchmark pull disjoint conversations from the
# dataset (first ``warmup_count`` vs. the rest).
```

That is the same defect #1641 fixed for the single-turn closed-loop path: the barrier drains server occupancy to zero, so the measured phase releases its first `parallel` requests within one event-loop tick against an idle server. Their TTFT carries a start-up burst that never recurs, and the reported percentiles treat that mixture as one distribution. On single-turn this overstated `p99` by **4.19x** (measured: 1609 ms reported vs 384 ms steady-state).

Multi-turn has a second, independent problem that single-turn does not: warmup and benchmark pull **disjoint** conversations, so every benchmark conversation still pays a cold first-turn prefill inside the measured window.

## Proposed direction

Two layers, mirroring what upstream vLLM does in `benchmarks/multi_turn/benchmark_serving_multi_turn.py`:

1. **No barrier between warmup and the measured portion**, as in #1641 — each warmup completion hands its slot to a measured request instead of draining first.
2. **First-turn warmup semantics**: warmup sends only the first turn of each conversation and writes the real reply back into the context; the benchmark phase then reuses the same conversations starting from turn 2. Cold prefill lands entirely in the un-measured warmup. Upstream does this with `client_args._replace(skip_first_turn=False, max_turns=1)` followed by reusing the returned conversations.

Note that (2) only pays off when the server has prefix caching enabled; without it the turn-2 prompt is longer and the burst can be worse. That trade-off needs to be stated wherever it is documented.

## Explicitly not the fix

Staggering the worker spawn across a ramp window (proposed in #1547) was evaluated and rejected. It trades a burst at the start of the measured window for an under-loaded stretch *inside* it, and upstream vLLM has no spawn stagger in either `serve.py` or its multi-turn benchmark. Details in #1547.

title: [Bug][perf] JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string when parsing streamed SSE chunks under high concurrency
body:
## EvalScope 版本
1.10.0

## 工具
- [x] Perf

## 问题
`evalscope perf` 默认 `stream=true`。高并发（`parallel=256`）压 vLLM `/v1/completions` 时，偶发 1～2 条请求 Failed。服务端 HTTP 200，token 已正常生成。

最终摘要类似：`Total / Success / Failed = 1024 / 1022 / 2`。

栈在 `evalscope/perf/plugin/api/default_api.py` 的 `process_request`：

File ".../evalscope/perf/plugin/api/default_api.py", line 151, in process_request
    data = json.loads(chunk)
json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 176 (char 175)

`StreamedResponseHandler.add_chunk` 按 `\n\n` 切开后不再校验 JSON，半包事件被交给 `json.loads`，异常导致整条请求记失败。buffer 尾部的不完整 JSON 会 wait，但 `\n\n` 分割路径没有同样保护。

Not a duplicate of #1466：那是 `AttributeError`（把整段 SSE 当 str、非标准 Content-Type）。本问题是标准 `text/event-stream` 下 TCP 半包 JSON。

## 复现
vLLM 0.27.0 + 较长 `served-model-name` + `--stream` + `--parallel 256` + `--max-tokens 1024` + `--tokenize-prompt`（走 `/v1/completions`）。低并发 / 非流式很难复现。

## 建议
1. `\n\n` 切开后先 `json.loads`，失败则退回 buffer 等下一包；
2. 或 `process_request` 里捕获 `JSONDecodeError` 后 `continue`，不要把整条请求标 Failed。

title: Proposal: EvalPort adapter for portable benchmark datasets (Sample / BenchmarkMeta)
body:
Hi maintainers — I'm Sahi, maintainer of [EvalPort](https://github.com/adhabnr-ux/evalport), an open spec (JSON Schemas + Python/TS SDKs) for portable LLM eval test suites, test cases, and result sets. Read through `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s "Adding a New Benchmark" section and `evalscope/api/dataset`/`evalscope/api/benchmark` before writing this, so this is grounded in the actual adapter pattern rather than a generic pitch.

EvalScope's benchmark contract is genuinely clean: a `BenchmarkMeta(name=..., dataset_id=..., subset_list=..., metric_list=..., eval_split=...)` registered via `@register_benchmark`, paired with a `DataAdapter.record_to_sample()` that maps a raw dataset row to a `Sample`. That `record_to_sample -> Sample` boundary is basically the exact seam an EvalPort adapter needs.

Concretely, I think this could be a `evalscope/benchmarks/evalport/evalport_adapter.py` following your own documented pattern:

```python
from evalscope.api.benchmark import BenchmarkMeta, DefaultDataAdapter
from evalscope.api.dataset import Sample
from evalscope.api.registry import register_benchmark
from evalport_sdk import TestSuite

@register_benchmark(
    BenchmarkMeta(
        name='evalport',
        pretty_name='EvalPort Suite',
        dataset_id='local://path/to/suite.evalport.json',  # or a suite URL
        metric_list=['acc'],
        eval_split='test',
    )
)
class EvalPortAdapter(DefaultDataAdapter):
    def record_to_sample(self, record):
        # record is already an EvalPort TestCase dict — input/target map directly
        return Sample(input=record['input'], target=record['expected'])
```

...plus the inverse direction: exporting an EvalScope `Score`/`AggScore` run as an EvalPort ResultSet, so results are comparable across tools that also speak EvalPort (a few CLI harnesses have adopted it already).

Given EvalScope already evaluates LLM, VLM, and AIGC benchmarks with a registry that's designed for exactly this kind of pluggable adapter, this felt like a natural fit rather than a stretch. Spec: https://github.com/adhabnr-ux/evalport/blob/main/SPEC.md

No pressure — if this isn't a priority I understand, EvalScope has plenty going on. If it's interesting, I'm happy to send a PR that follows your Step 1-4 contribution flow (adapter dir, requirements.txt, docs) rather than just leaving this as talk. Thanks for the well-documented adapter pattern, it made this easy to scope.

title: Cross-project discussion: reproducibility, uncertainty and benchmark provenance
body:
We're studying EvalScope as one of the reference projects for BRONCO, a research-first AI-metrology effort focused on what an evaluation result can legitimately claim.

The areas we're working through include construct validity, provenance, repeatability/reproducibility, uncertainty, evaluator noise and contamination controls before strict rankings are treated as meaningful measurements.

EvalScope's broad evaluation infrastructure makes it a useful reality check for that work.

If maintainers or contributors are interested, I'd genuinely welcome criticism or cross-project collaboration instead of building another isolated evaluation stack.
